items.title: Intel Stock Drops After $15 Billion Share Sale. Is AI Spending Getting Too Expensive?
items.summary: Intel just chose to sell $15 billion worth of its own stock rather than borrow more money, and shareholders are already paying the price. The question hanging over the entire AI infrastructure boom is whether anyone building it will ever generate enough cash to justify the cost.

items.title: Why Micron is Decisively Better Positioned Than Intel Now
items.summary: Both Micron and Intel just reported earnings that crushed expectations, but one company is locking in guaranteed billion-dollar AI contracts while the other is still waiting for its first external foundry customer to sign.
